subject: Updated subprocessor inventory & SCCs — Acme Payments request
messages:
From: Anita Sharma <anita.sharma@acmepayments.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmepayments.com
Date: 2028-01-09T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Vendor subprocessor inventory and SCCs for Acme Payments review

Hi Kimberly,

We're kicking off the security/third-party review for Redwood as part of our production onboarding. Legal and Procurement asked for a consolidated subprocessor inventory that includes: role (storage/telemetry/keys), country of processing, whether they have access to plaintext, and any cross-border transfer pathways (esp. transfers to the US).

Can you also confirm whether Redwood relies on:
- any subprocessors in Russia/China or other sanctioned jurisdictions
- third-party analytics vendors that persist customer request logs outside the EU
- a hosted KMS/HSM provider (name + region) vs customer-managed keys

We have attached our vendor data map (Acme_Vendor_Data_Map.xlsx). For contract/legal next steps, our counsel wants to execute a DPA addendum (DocuSign preferred) and confirm the use of EU SCCs + UK addendum for transfers. Please point us to the inventory and any SCC/UK Addendum packet.

We aim to close this by 2028-01-20 for our compliance window. Would appreciate an initial inventory and a short note on any temporary/short-lived processors that we should be aware of.

Thanks,
Anita Sharma
Head of Vendor Risk — Acme Payments

Attachment: Acme_Vendor_Data_Map.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Anita Sharma <anita.sharma@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-09T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Vendor subprocessor inventory and SCCs for Acme Payments review

Anita — thanks for the note and the workbook. We're on it.

High-level: Redwood uses SCCs (EU Standard Contractual Clauses) + the UK Addendum for EU/UK customer transfers. For customers that require customer-managed keys we support a bring-your-own-key model (BYOK) with an HSM-backed provider; otherwise we use our managed KMS. I'll loop in Jordan and Rishi for the inventory and the KMS specifics.

Attached is a first snapshot (subprocessors_snapshot_2028-01-09.pdf) — it's high-level and I'm asking the infra team for the CSV export with mapping to access rights and residency. We'll follow up with a definitive inventory and timeline for any temporary processors.

I'll also include our DocuSign DPA addendum link once legal publishes the packet.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Contracts Manager — Redwood Inference

Attachment: subprocessors_snapshot_2028-01-09.pdf (PDF)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Anita Sharma <anita.sharma@acmepayments.com>
Date: 2028-01-10T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Vendor subprocessor inventory and SCCs for Acme Payments review — infra details

Team / Anita — collected details from infra and privacy: please see the quick answers below and the attached CSV for a row-level inventory. I'll highlight any items that may require a short-term mitigation plan.

Short answers:
- Sanctioned jurisdictions: No active subprocessors in Russia/China/Iran. We have edge partners in APAC for latency but not for EU customer request processing.
- KMS/HSM: Redwood managed KMS (KeySafe, eu-central-1) for managed keys. BYOK/HSM is supported via KeySafe HSMs in FR and DE (customer-managed option).
- Telemetry/observability: TelemetryX (US/EU) — logs are routed to eu-west-1 for EU customers by default; TelemetryX retains aggregated metrics in the US for product analytics but raw request logs for EU customers stay in EU unless a customer opts into global analytics.
- Transit/proxy: TransitBridge (US infra) is our primary transit relay; we maintain an EU onshore fallback (TransitBridge-EU) for customers who require exclusive EU routing.
- Temporary analytics: Pulselytics (contracted for a pilot) is scheduled for decommissioning — exit target 2028-01-25. It's only used for synthetic load tests and flagged in the CSV.

Action items for Acme:
1) I will attach the CSV export: subprocessor_inventory_2028-01-10.csv (includes role, country, access_level, data_path, contractual basis).
2) Kimberly: share DocuSign DPA addendum link when ready.
3) Lauren: please prepare the note for Legal on SCC+UK Addendum + our supplementary measures (encryption at rest, contractual restrictions, onshore fallback).

Jordan Blake
Senior Cloud Ops — Redwood Inference

Attachment: subprocessor_inventory_2028-01-10.csv (CSV)

Thanks Jordan — that's helpful. A couple of quick clarifications we need to close on our side:

1) Pulselytics timeline: can you confirm that there will be no persistence of live customer request logs outside the EU prior to 2028-01-25? If there is any short window where test traffic or persisted logs exist in the US please confirm retention policy and deletion plan.

2) DocuSign DPA addendum: please send the DocuSign link and (if possible) a brief paragraph we can include in our procurement write-up stating the contractual basis for transfers (SCC + technical measures + onshore fallback).

If we can get those details by EOD 2028-01-12 we can stay on track for our 2028-01-20 compliance cutoff.

Best,
Anita
Head of Vendor Risk — Acme Payments

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-01-18T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Final inventory & SCC statement — Redwood + Acme Payments

Anita — apologies for the short delay; please find the finalized materials attached. Summary below and next steps.

Summary: 
- Pulselytics: Confirmed no persistence of live customer request logs outside EU. Any synthetic test data that transiently crossed into our US analytics pipeline has been deleted; infra has issued a retention wipe and audit snapshot. Exit target remains 2028-01-25 and we've included a short exit certificate in the CSV.
- KMS/HSM: Managed KeySafe (eu-central-1) used for managed keys. BYOK/HSM supported via KeySafe HSMs in FR/DE. Additional note: we can provide an HSM attestation excerpt on request.
- Transfers & Contracts: Redwood executes EU SCCs + UK Addendum by default for transfers. Supplementary measures: encryption at rest (AES-256), TLS in transit, limited admin access logs, and contractual constraints on subprocessors. We will include a one-paragraph transfer rationale for your procurement doc: "Redwood Inference relies on the EU Standard Contractual Clauses and the UK Addendum for transfers of personal data from the EEA/UK to third countries, supplemented by technical measures (encryption in transit and at rest) and documented onshore fallback routing for customers requiring exclusive regional residency."

Attachments included: subprocessors_snapshot_2028-01-18.pdf (updated inventory with exit certificates), subprocessor_inventory_2028-01-10.csv (row-level export), and the DocuSign link for the DPA addendum below.
